claim: Ciona cardiopharyngeal progenitors migrate as cohesive bilateral cell pairs polarized along the leader-trailer migration path while moving between the ventral epidermis and trunk endoderm.
source: The Ciona cardiopharyngeal progenitors provide the simplest model of collective cell migration, with cohesive bilateral cell pairs polarized along the leader-trailer migration path while moving between the ventral epidermis and trunk endoderm.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and is supported by experimental observations described throughout the manuscript, including microscopy data showing cell pair arrangements.

claim: Cardiopharyngeal progenitors maintain supracellular polarity with differential distributions of protrusive forces, cell-matrix adhesion, and myosin-based retraction forces along the leader-trailer axis.
source: Combining computational modeling, confocal microscopy, and molecular perturbations, we identify cardiopharyngeal progenitors as the simplest cell collective maintaining supracellular polarity with differential distributions of protrusive forces, cell-matrix adhesion, and myosin-based retraction forces along the leader-trailer axis.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational modeling predictions, confocal microscopy observations, and molecular perturbation experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Cell-cell communication helps establish a hierarchy to align collective polarity with the direction of migration.
source: 4D simulations and experimental observations suggest that cell-cell communication helps establish a hierarchy to align collective polarity with the direction of migration, as observed with three or more cells in silico and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by both computational simulations and experimental observations of cells migrating in groups of three or more.

claim: Cell pairs are more persistent than single cells, migrating longer distances and presumably with higher accuracy.
source: Our approach reveals emerging properties of the migrating collective: cell pairs are more persistent, migrating longer distances, and presumably with higher accuracy.
evidence: This claim is supported by both simulation results and experimental observations comparing cell pairs to single cells.

claim: Cell pairs can overcome mechanical resistance of the trunk endoderm more effectively when they are polarized collectively.
source: Simulations suggest that cell pairs can overcome mechanical resistance of the trunk endoderm more effectively when they are polarized collectively.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations that model the interaction between migrating cells and the endoderm.

claim: Polarized supracellular organization of cardiopharyngeal progenitors confers emergent physical properties that determine mechanical interactions with their environment during morphogenesis.
source: We propose that polarized supracellular organization of cardiopharyngeal progenitors confers emergent physical properties that determine mechanical interactions with their environment during morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a proposed conclusion based on the combined computational and experimental findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: The leader cell extends dynamic lamellipodia-like protrusions while the posterior trailer terminates in a tapered retractive edge.
source: The anterior leader cell extends dynamic lamellipodia-like protrusions, while the posterior trailer terminates in a tapered retractive edge (Christiaen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction and is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Under unperturbed conditions, the migrating TVCs remain committed to their leader/trailer positions.
source: Under unperturbed conditions, the migrating TVCs remain committed to their leader/trailer positions (Gline et al., 2015; Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TVCs contact multiple tissues during migration, including the posterior mesenchyme, the trunk endoderm, and the ventral epidermis, which serves as substrate.
source: TVCs contact multiple tissues during migration, including the posterior mesenchyme, the trunk endoderm, and the ventral epidermis, which serves as substrate (Gline et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Single migrating TVCs generally display morphologies intermediate to those of either leader or trailer, generating both a leading edge and a retracting rear end.
source: Single migrating TVCs generally display morphologies intermediate to those of either leader or trailer, generating both a leading edge and a retracting rear end, thus producing overall shapes similar to migrating pairs (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations and comparison of cell shapes shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: Both single cells and cell pairs maintain similar overall shapes as measured by aspect ratios.
source: This comparison shows that both maintain similar overall shapes (Figure 1C), leading us to hypothesize that similar force distribution profiles may exist in both conditions.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Narrowly focused retractive forces cause aberrant widening of the leading edge and fail to produce the tapered rear in simulations.
source: By varying the width of the angular segment for retraction forces at the rear, we observed that narrowly focused retractive forces cause aberrant widening of the leading edge and fail to produce the tapered rear (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, bottom row), suggesting that a broadly retracting trailing edge better accounts for the observed shapes of single cells.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The single-cell shape is faithfully reproduced if the retraction force is centripetal, radially converging to the cell center along the width and heights of the rear half of the cell.
source: Simulations showed that the single-cell shape is faithfully reproduced if the retraction force is centripetal, radially converging to the cell center along the width and heights of the rear half of the cell.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations.

claim: Protrusion force is centrifugal in the front half of the cell, diverging from the cell center.
source: Similarly, protrusion force is centrifugal in the front half of the cell, diverging from the cell center (Figure 1D, Video 1).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 1D and Video 1.

claim: Computationally stitching two identical single-cell models failed to reproduce the polarized morphology of migrating pairs.
source: Although single TVC migration (Gline et al., 2015) suggests that individual TVCs are migration-competent and do not require a cell partner, computationally stitching two identical single-cell models failed to reproduce the polarized morphology of migrating pairs.
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling results.

claim: When simulated leader and trailer cells were endowed with equivalent protrusive activity, the width of the trailer front extended beyond the width of the leader posterior.
source: Specifically, when simulated leader and trailer cells were endowed with equivalent protrusive activity, the width of the trailer front extended beyond the width of the leader posterior, a morphology not observed in control embryos (Figure 1E, yellow two-headed arrow).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Equivalent protrusive activity in leader and trailer caused the simulated trailer to leave its posterior position and travel side-by-side with the leader.
source: This also impacted collective polarity, causing the simulated trailer to leave its posterior position and travel side-by-side with the leader (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The typical leader TVC has a wide leading edge with lamellipodia-like protrusions that depend on Rhod/f- and Cdc42-controlled actin networks.
source: The predicted leader-dominated protrusive activity of the cell pair was consistent with previous observations that the typical leader TVC has a wide leading edge with lamellipodia-like protrusions that depend on Rhod/f- and Cdc42-controlled actin networks (Christiaen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Experimentally increasing protrusive activity in one or both migrating cells disrupted their collective polarity, with cells more likely to migrate in parallel.
source: Under these conditions, experimentally increasing protrusive activity in one or both migrating cells disrupted their collective polarity, with cells more likely to migrate in parallel as predicted by in silico simulations (Figure 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E that matches computational predictions.

claim: Protrusive activity is suppressed in trailer cells compared to leader and single cells.
source: This result suggests that the protrusive activity is suppressed in trailer cells compared to leader and single cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the combined computational and experimental results.

claim: Simulations that reduce protrusive activity in the trailer without increasing its retractile forces cause the leader to detach and move forward on its own.
source: Nevertheless, simulations that reduce protrusive activity in the trailer without increasing its retractile forces cause the leader to detach and move forward on its own, overcoming significant mutual adhesion between the two cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Some protrusive activity in the trailer is still required for paired TVC migration.
source: This suggests that some protrusive activity in the trailer is still required, and that, in paired TVCs, the cells exert equivalent forces, while coordinating their activities to distribute protrusive and retractile forces to the leader and trailer cells, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–E).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from computational simulations.

claim: The best computational recapitulation of observed shapes was achieved with centripetal retractive forces dominating in the trailer and centrifugal protrusive forces in the leader.
source: Next, we sought to further probe the supracellular model using phenomenological observations. Notably, the best computational recapitulation of observed shapes was achieved with centripetal retractive forces dominating in the trailer, pulling the cell rear forward and down, while the centrifugal protrusive forces in the leader pushed the front forward (Figure 1B and D, Video 2).
evidence: This claim is based on computational modeling results shown in Figure 1B and D.

claim: iMyo-GFP accumulates at the rear of the trailer cell and is relatively depleted from the leader-trailer junction.
source: Consistent with the model's prediction of a trailer-polarized retractile activity, we observe that iMyo-GFP, an intrabody that recognizes non-muscle myosin II through a conserved epitope (Chaigne et al., 2013; Hashimoto et al., 2015), accumulates at the rear of the trailer cell and is relatively depleted from the leader-trailer junction (Figure 1F, Figure 1—figure supplement 3), implying that the retraction in the trailer is dominant, while the retractive force in the leader is weak, lending further support to the hypothesis that TVC pairs migrate as a supracellular collective.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 1F and Figure 1—figure supplement 3, and citations to previous work on the iMyo-GFP marker.

claim: Pairs of multipotent cardiopharyngeal progenitors migrate as a polarized supracellular collective, with protrusive activity and myosin-based retraction distributed across leader and trailer cells, respectively.
source: Taken together, our computational predictions and experimental observations support a model where pairs of multipotent cardiopharyngeal progenitors migrate as a polarized supracellular collective, with protrusive activity and myosin-based retraction distributed across leader and trailer cells, respectively.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the combined computational and experimental findings.

claim: Cell-matrix interactions and distribution of protrusive activity to the leading TVC result in the generation of a broad leading edge during the establishment of collective TVC polarity.
source: Cell-matrix interactions and distribution of protrusive activity to the leading TVC result in the generation of a broad leading edge during the establishment of collective TVC polarity (Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Conditions that perturb cell-matrix adhesion often increase the sphericity of leading cells, suggesting that they fail to establish flattened protrusions at the leading edge.
source: Conditions that perturb cell-matrix adhesion often increase the sphericity of leading cells, suggesting that they fail to establish flattened protrusions at the leading edge (Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: TVCs' sphericities did not differ at stage 19, suggesting that they are born with equivalent shapes.
source: TVCs' sphericities did not differ at stage 19, suggesting that they are born with equivalent shapes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental measurements of cell sphericity at different developmental stages.

claim: Cell sphericities begin to differ significantly during migration, indicating establishment of leader/trailer polarity, adoption of distinct states, and orientation in direction of migration.
source: Cell sphericities begin to differ significantly during migration, indicating establishment of leader/trailer polarity, adoption of distinct states (Figure 2A), and orientation in direction of migration.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Collective TVC polarization is abolished by disruption of cell-matrix adhesion by misexpression of a dominant-negative version of the collagen receptor, Discoidin domain receptor (Ddrdn).
source: Collective TVC polarization is abolished by disruption of cell-matrix adhesion by misexpression of a dominant-negative version of the collagen receptor, Discoidin domain receptor (Ddrdn), which alters integrin-mediated cell-matrix adhesion and disrupts polarized Bmp-Smad signaling (Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: In simulations, the cell with reduced adhesion was more likely to assume the trailer position.
source: In these conditions, the cell with reduced adhesion was more likely to assume the trailer position (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Coexpression of Intß1dn increased the proportion of labeled trailer cells to 57% in mosaic embryos.
source: In contrast, coexpression of Intß1dn increased the proportion of labeled trailer cells to 57% in mosaic embryos (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cells that inherited Ddrdn were significantly more likely to be in the trailer position, increasing the proportion of mCherry-labeled cells in the trailer position to 66%.
source: Cells that inherited Ddrdn were significantly more likely to be in the trailer position, increasing the proportion of mCherry-labeled cells in the trailer position to 66% (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Mosaic expression of RhoDFca has the opposite, albeit not statistically significant, effect, promoting positioning of the labeled cell anteriorly.
source: Mosaic expression of RhoDFca has the opposite, albeit not statistically significant, effect, promoting positioning of the labeled cell anteriorly (Figure 2C), further lending support to our hypothesis of leader cells being more protrusive and less retractive than trailers.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Reduced cell-matrix adhesion promotes positioning of the cell with reduced adhesion posterior to the cell with more adhesion, thereby preferentially adopting the trailer state.
source: Taken together, these observations indicate that reduced cell-matrix adhesion promotes positioning of the cell with reduced adhesion posterior to the cell with more adhesion, thereby preferentially adopting the trailer state, which in turn suggests that cell-matrix adhesion is stronger in leader cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined computational and experimental results.

claim: Leader cells consistently contained more ventral Lifeact::GFP+ F-actin puncta than trailer cells.
source: Quantifications indicated that leader cells consistently contained more ventral Lifeact::GFP+ F-actin puncta than trailer cells, supporting the prediction that F-actin-rich adhesion complexes are enriched in leading cells during TVC migration (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Increased cell-matrix adhesion and protrusive activity are hallmarks of the leader cell state during collective cell migration.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that increased cell-matrix adhesion and protrusive activity are hallmarks of the leader cell state during collective cell migration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results.

claim: The two cells are not arranged in a linear leader-trailer orientation at birth.
source: However, the two cells are not arranged in a linear leader-trailer orientation at birth (Figure 3A), and previous observations indicated that either cell can assume a leader position, although single-cell lineage tracing indicates that the leader emerges from the most anterior cell in ~95% of embryos (Gline et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 3A and a citation to previous work.

claim: Single-cell lineage tracing indicates that the leader emerges from the most anterior cell in ~95% of embryos.
source: However, the two cells are not arranged in a linear leader-trailer orientation at birth (Figure 3A), and previous observations indicated that either cell can assume a leader position, although single-cell lineage tracing indicates that the leader emerges from the most anterior cell in ~95% of embryos (Gline et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Prior to migration at embryonic stage 17, the leader/trailer axis is more orthogonal to the future direction of anterior movement.
source: Tracking cos(θ) to quantify the alignment of cell pairs with direction of migration, with θ defined as the angle between the leader-trailer axis (axis connecting their centers of mass) and the direction of migration (Figure 3A and B), shows that prior to migration at embryonic stage 17 (8.5 hr post fertilization [hpf]), the leader/trailer axis is more orthogonal to the future direction of anterior movement.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: The cells reach their full polarization and alignment with direction of migration by stage 21, a process that takes approximately 1.5 hr at 18°C.
source: The cells reach their full polarization and alignment with direction of migration by stage 21, a process that takes approximately 1.5 hr at 18°C, after which they continue to migrate as a fully polarized cell pair for approximately 2 hr (Figure 3A and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 3A and C.

claim: Either the faster-slower or leader-trailer mode led cells to rearrange into a single file aligned with the migration path.
source: By contrast, either the faster-slower or leader-trailer mode led cells to rearrange into a single file aligned with the migration path (i.e., cos(θ) = 1), with the leader-trailer mode allowing faster alignment, with a half-time to alignment reduced compared to the fast-slower mode (Figure 3D, Video 4).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 3D and Video 4.

claim: The leader-trailer mode allows faster alignment compared to the faster-slower mode.
source: By contrast, either the faster-slower or leader-trailer mode led cells to rearrange into a single file aligned with the migration path (i.e., cos(θ) = 1), with the leader-trailer mode allowing faster alignment, with a half-time to alignment reduced compared to the fast-slower mode (Figure 3D, Video 4).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 3D and Video 4.

claim: In three-cell simulations with the independent mode, cells failed to produce linear arrangements and remained in triangular formation.
source: Similar to two-cell simulations, the independent mode failed to produce linear arrangements and the cells remained in triangular formation with no leader emerging, potentially due to the three-cell system minimizing the adhesive energy when each cell maintains contacts with the other two (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The leader-middle-trailer mode was the most effective at producing full polarization and linear order rapidly in three-cell simulations.
source: The leader-middle-trailer mode was again the most effective at producing full polarization and linear order rapidly (Figure 3E, Video 6), suggesting that basic hierarchical rules of collective polarization can produce linear arrangements of cell groups containing variable numbers of cells.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 3E and Video 6.

claim: In conditions with ectopic FGF/M-Ras/Mek-driven induction, the cells align in the direction of movement in 57% of the experimental embryos.
source: In conditions such as misexpression of a constitutively active form of M-Ras using the Mesp enhancer (Razy-Krajka et al., 2018) (Mesp>M-Rasca), the cells align in the direction of movement in 57% of the experimental embryos, with a single anterior leader, followed by two (13%) or three (87%) cells arranged in a single line (68%, n = 31) (Figure 3F, Videos 7 and 8).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F and Videos 7 and 8, with a citation to previous work.

claim: Increasing or decreasing cell-cell adhesion energy causes the cell-cell boundary area to increase or decrease, respectively.
source: Multiple simulations varying the cell-cell adhesion energy in our basic model show that cell-cell adhesion strength does not affect the total displacement of cell pairs over long time intervals (Figure 3G, bottom right). However, increasing or decreasing cell-cell adhesion energy causes the cell-cell boundary area to increase or decrease, respectively (Figure 3G, top right, blue plot), which leads to a drastic misalignment of cells with the direction of migration beyond a cell-cell adhesion strength of 10 (relative energy units).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Cells with high cell-cell adhesion will reorient their supracellular polarity away from the direction of migration.
source: This suggests that the extent of cell-cell adhesion may be regulated in vivo and that cells with high cell-cell adhesion will reorient their supracellular polarity away from the direction of migration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from computational simulations.

claim: TVCs move at ~0.4 µm/min, which is relatively slow compared to specialized motile cells.
source: Unlike specialized motile cells, such as Dictyostelium, fish keratocytes, or neutrophils, which can migrate at ~10 µm/min, 7.5 μm/min, and ~19 μm/min, respectively (Buenemann et al., 2010; Graham et al., 2013; Hoang et al., 2013), TVCs move at ~0.4 µm/min, which is relatively slow, but not unexpected for a developmental migration that contributes to the establishment of accurate cellular patterns in the embryo (Trepat et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work on cell migration speeds.

claim: In simulations, motile cell pairs are always more persistent than single cells when centers of mass are tracked over time.
source: In simulations, motile cell pairs are always more persistent than single cells when centers of mass are tracked over time for each condition, suggesting that single cells are more sensitive to directional stochasticity.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations.

claim: The total length of the migration path in the simulations was not altered, suggesting that the decreased displacement is a function of the meandering path traveled by the less persistent single cells.
source: Of note, the total length of the migration path in the simulations was not altered, suggesting that the decreased displacement is a function of the meandering path traveled by the less persistent single cells (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from computational simulations shown in Figure 4B.

claim: In agreement with simulations, TVC pairs migrated further from the anterior ATM than single cells in vivo.
source: We compared the final displacement of single TVCs in vivo to the total displacement of the leader TVC. In agreement with simulations, TVC pairs migrated further from the anterior ATM than single cells (Gline et al., 2015; Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C and a citation to previous work.

claim: In control conditions, the leader and trailer migrate with similar persistence.
source: In control conditions, the leader and trailer migrate with similar persistence; however, the migration paths of single TVCs were significantly less persistent than those of either leader or trailer cells, suggesting that in vivo, collective organization confers robust directionality to the migrating cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: The migration paths of single TVCs were significantly less persistent than those of either leader or trailer cells.
source: In control conditions, the leader and trailer migrate with similar persistence; however, the migration paths of single TVCs were significantly less persistent than those of either leader or trailer cells, suggesting that in vivo, collective organization confers robust directionality to the migrating cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations.

claim: Collective organization confers robust directionality to the migrating cells in vivo.
source: In control conditions, the leader and trailer migrate with similar persistence; however, the migration paths of single TVCs were significantly less persistent than those of either leader or trailer cells, suggesting that in vivo, collective organization confers robust directionality to the migrating cells.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental observations.

claim: Both simulations and in vivo observations suggested that polarized cell pairs migrate with increased robustness to fluctuations in directionality compared to single cells.
source: In summary, both simulations and in vivo observations suggested that polarized cell pairs migrate with increased robustness to fluctuations in directionality compared to single cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the combined computational and experimental findings.

claim: Shortly after the onset of migration, the TVCs penetrate the extracellular space between the ventral trunk epidermis and the softer trunk endoderm, which locally deforms as TVCs progress anteriorly.
source: Specifically, shortly after the onset of migration, the TVCs penetrate the extracellular space between the ventral trunk epidermis, which they use as stiff substrate, and the softer trunk endoderm, which locally deforms as TVCs progress anteriorly (Gline et al., 2015; Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations shown in Figure 5A and a citation to previous work.

claim: The trunk endoderm likely exerts mechanical resistance to the passage of the TVCs.
source: We reasoned that the trunk endoderm likely exerts mechanical resistance to the passage of the TVCs and hypothesized that this resistance may be better overcome by polarized cell pairs (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on observations and reasoning.

claim: When two cells migrate in a leader-trailer arrangement, the surface that the leader exposes to mechanical resistance is equivalent to that of a single cell, while the trailer pushes from the rear, therefore adding forward-bearing compression force to overcome endoderm resistance.
source: We predicted that when two cells migrate in a leader-trailer arrangement, the surface that the leader exposes to mechanical resistance is equivalent to that of a single cell, while the trailer pushes from the rear, therefore adding forward-bearing compression force to overcome endoderm resistance (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a prediction based on reasoning and illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: When modeling a softer endoderm, polarized cell pairs perform best, whether in supracellular mode or equivalent force distribution, while side-by-side cells were the slowest.
source: When modeling a softer endoderm, by modulating volume preservation and cortical tension parameters relative to those of the TVCs (see Appendix 1), polarized cell pairs perform best, whether in supracellular mode or equivalent force distribution, while side-by-side cells were the slowest, presumably because they expose a greater surface to mechanical resistance (Figure 5B and D).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 5B and D.

claim: Two equivalent cells moving in single file advanced marginally faster than the supracellular pair when modeling a softer endoderm.
source: Notably, two equivalent cells moving in single file advanced marginally faster than the supracellular pair, suggesting that cell alignment itself is a key determinant of efficient migration under the soft tissue.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations.

claim: When simulating a stiffer endoderm, the advantage of supracellular organization became more apparent, with the supracellular collective migrating faster than other arrangements.
source: When simulating a stiffer endoderm, the advantage of supracellular organization became more apparent. In these simulations, the supracellular collective migrated faster than other arrangements (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Cells migrating side-by-side were slower than single cells with either endoderm stiffness.
source: Notably, cells migrating side-by-side were slower than single cells with either endoderm stiffness (Figure 5D), which is consistent with the notion that a more extended surface of contact with the endoderm exposes them to greater mechanical resistance, while the smooth teardrop shape of single cells may be near optimal for lowering the resistive deformations of the endoderm.
evidence: This claim is based on computational simulations shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The collective shape resulting from supracellular organization optimally minimizes mechanical resistance of the surrounding tissue to migration.
source: This suggests that the collective shape resulting from supracellular organization optimally minimizes mechanical resistance of the surrounding tissue to migration.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from computational simulations.

claim: In vivo, the interactions between TVCs and endoderm cells are likely more complex, involving indirect cell-cell signaling via extracellular deposition of collagen9-a1 by the endoderm.
source: The predicted relative speeds of cells migrating under the endoderm are based on the simplest model, which assumes that the endoderm's primary effect is mechanical resistance to deformation. In vivo, the interactions between TVCs and endoderm cells are likely more complex, involving indirect cell-cell signaling via extracellular deposition of collagen9-a1 by the endoderm (Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The collective organization of migrating cardiopharyngeal progenitors allows them to overcome mechanical resistance from the deforming endoderm and reach a typically mesodermal position between germ layers for cardiac organogenesis.
source: In summary, the combined in silico simulations and in vivo observations indicate that the collective organization of migrating cardiopharyngeal progenitors allows them to overcome mechanical resistance from the deforming endoderm and reach a typically mesodermal position between germ layers for cardiac organogenesis.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the combined computational and experimental findings.

claim: Ciona is a simple chordate among the closest relatives of vertebrates.
source: We use the cardiogenic lineage of the tunicate Ciona, a simple chordate among the closest relatives of vertebrates (Dehal and Boore, 2006; Putnam et al., 2008), to develop and test a computational model of collective polarity and directed cell migration.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: During Ciona embryonic development, the cardiopharyngeal precursors are born as two superficially equivalent cells arising from the division of bilateral founders.
source: During Ciona embryonic development, the cardiopharyngeal precursors are born as two superficially equivalent cells arising from the division of bilateral founders.
evidence: This is a description of the developmental biology of Ciona.

claim: The resulting cells migrate from their origin in the tail to the ventral trunk, hence their denomination as trunk ventral cells (aka TVCs).
source: The resulting cells migrate from their origin in the tail to the ventral trunk, hence their denomination as trunk ventral cells (aka TVCs) (Christiaen et al., 2008; Gline et al., 2015; Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: The TVCs migrate as pairs, offering the simplest possible model of polarized collective cell migration.
source: The TVCs migrate as pairs, offering the simplest possible model of polarized collective cell migration.
evidence: This is a characterization of the TVC system as a model.

claim: TVCs maintain polarized organization along the anterior posterior axis and spheroid shapes as they invade the extracellular space between the epidermis and the endoderm.
source: TVCs maintain polarized organization along the anterior posterior axis and spheroid shapes as they invade the extracellular space between the epidermis and the endoderm.
evidence: This is a description of TVC behavior during migration.

claim: Ciona TVCs represent a simple and intriguing model to study the mechanics and polarity of cells migrating in an embryonic context.
source: Ciona TVCs thus represent a simple and intriguing model to study the mechanics and polarity of cells migrating in an embryonic context (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a characterization of the TVC system as a model.

claim: CPM is advantageous in modeling the TVC pair as it allows reproduction of both the detailed evolving 3D shapes of motile cells and the deformation of tissues surrounding these cells over a reasonable computational time.
source: CPM is advantageous in modeling the TVC pair as it allows us to reproduce both the detailed evolving 3D shapes of motile cells and the deformation of tissues surrounding these cells over a reasonable computational time (Thüroff et al., 2019; Rens and Edelstein-Keshet, 2019; Fortuna et al., 2020) – one of the more challenging tasks for detailed force-balance models in 3D (Wu et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work on CPM modeling.

claim: Cell morphology reflects and conditions cellular behavior, inasmuch as both emerge from underlying mechanical forces.
source: Cell morphology reflects and conditions cellular behavior, inasmuch as both emerge from underlying mechanical forces (Figure 1A; Mogilner and Keren, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: Cell shape provides a phenomenological proxy to biophysical forces driving cellular behavior.
source: From that standpoint, cell shape provides a phenomenological proxy to biophysical forces driving cellular behavior (Campàs et al., 2014; Maitre, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: In migrating collectives, leader cells typically adopt splayed morphologies with protrusive activity at the leading edge, while trailing cells display a tapered rear.
source: In migrating collectives, leader cells typically adopt splayed morphologies with protrusive activity at the leading edge, while trailing cells display a tapered rear (Nabeshima et al., 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: A purely mechanical model such as CPM, which assumes that most active stresses are generated at the cellular periphery in addition to hydrostatic pressure in the cytoplasm, can uncover the biomechanical underpinnings of collective cell shape and movement.
source: This illustrates that a purely mechanical model such as CPM, which assumes that most active stresses are generated at the cellular periphery in addition to hydrostatic pressure in the cytoplasm, can uncover the biomechanical underpinnings of collective cell shape and movement.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the modeling results.

claim: The distribution of various cytoskeletal activities across all cells in a collective suggests the existence of mechanisms to ensure such 'division of labor.'
source: However, in the 'supracell,' the distribution of various cytoskeletal activities across all cells in a collective suggests the existence of mechanisms to ensure such 'division of labor.'
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the modeling results.

claim: Cell-cell adhesion must be strong enough to maintain the integrity of the collective and permit mechanical coupling.
source: First and foremost, cell-cell adhesion must be strong enough to maintain the integrity of the collective and permit mechanical coupling, lest cells lose contact and migrate disjointly (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the modeling results shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The model predicts that excessive cell-cell adhesion antagonizes cell-matrix adhesion and disrupts collective polarity.
source: Conversely, the model predicts that excessive cell-cell adhesion antagonizes cell-matrix adhesion and disrupts collective polarity.
evidence: This is a prediction from the computational model.

claim: Balancing cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion may result from either mechanical interaction, as suggested by the model, and/or biochemical cross-talks, as observed in other systems.
source: Balancing cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion may result from either mechanical interaction, as suggested by the model, and/or biochemical cross-talks, as observed in other systems (Martinez-Rico et al., 2010; Ramprasad et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim combines model predictions with citations to previous work on adhesion cross-talk.

claim: The coexistence and contributions of both cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion to supracellular migration emphasize the hybrid nature of such multicellular systems, where cells adopt intermediate states on an epithelial-to-mesenchymal continuum.
source: The coexistence and contributions of both cell-cell and cell-matrix adhesion to supracellular migration emphasize the hybrid nature of such multicellular systems, where cells adopt intermediate states on an epithelial-to-mesenchymal continuum (Friedl and Mayor, 2017; Bernadskaya and Christiaen, 2016; Lecaudey and Gilmour, 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Ciona cardiopharyngeal progenitors appear to focus contractility at the back of the trailer cell, suggesting that a 'rear-wheel' engine may help power their migration.
source: For instance, similar to Xenopus cranial neural crest cells and the zebrafish lateral line primordium (Yamaguchi, 2021), Ciona cardiopharyngeal progenitors appear to focus contractility at the back of the trailer cell, thus suggesting that a 'rear-wheel' engine may help power their migration.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work and comparison to other systems.

claim: In contrast to neural crest cells and Drosophila border cells, there is no exchange of cell positions between TVCs.
source: However, in contrast to neural crest cells and Drosophila border cells, we did not observe supracellular actomyosin 'cables' extending across cardiopharyngeal progenitors and there is no exchange of cell positions between TVCs.
evidence: This is a statement of what was not observed in the experiments.

claim: This 'rear-wheel' drive represents a back-to-front mechanical input, which propagates as compression force and emerges from rear-localized myosin activity, possibly in response to chemorepulsive inputs integrated by the trailer.
source: Instead, we surmise that this 'rear-wheel' drive represents a back-to-front mechanical input, which propagates as compression force and emerges from rear-localized myosin activity, possibly in response to chemorepulsive inputs integrated by the trailer.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observations and modeling results.

claim: It is conceivable that cell-cell adhesion complexes suppress myosin-based contractility at the back of the leader cell, for example, through recruitment of Rho GAP molecules by cadherin, as is the case in early Caenorhabditis elegans embryos.
source: It is also conceivable that cell-cell adhesion complexes suppress myosin-based contractility at the back of the leader cell, for example, through recruitment of Rho GAP molecules by cadherin, as is the case in early Caenorhabditis elegans embryos (Klompstra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis supported by a citation to work in another system.

claim: In neural crest cells, CIL provides back-to-front signals that polarize the cell collective, in part through cadherins, ephrin receptors, and planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway molecules.
source: In neural crest cells, CIL provides such back-to-front signals that polarize the cell collective, in part through cadherins, ephrin receptors, and planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway molecules (Mayor and Etienne-Manneville, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The PCP pathway offers a particularly tantalizing explanation for the spontaneous alignment of three or four adhering cells following ectopic induction of the cardiopharyngeal progenitor fate.
source: The PCP pathway offers a particularly tantalizing explanation for the spontaneous alignment of three or four adhering cells following ectopic induction of the cardiopharyngeal progenitor fate, and the existence of a 'leader-trailer' mode of collective arrangement predicted by the model.
evidence: This is a speculative hypothesis.

claim: TVCs' collective polarity is marked by higher protrusive activity and cell-matrix adhesion in the leader, as indicated by experimental observations and model predictions.
source: TVCs' collective polarity is marked by higher protrusive activity and cell-matrix adhesion in the leader, as indicated by experimental observations and model predictions (Christiaen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations, model predictions, and a citation to previous work.

claim: It is likely that adhesion complexes are established following lamellipodia formation and support traction forces, which complement rear-driven compression to propel the cells forward.
source: Mechanically, it is likely that adhesion complexes are established following lamellipodia formation and support traction forces, which complement rear-driven compression to propel the cells forward.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on mechanical reasoning.

claim: Lower protrusive activity in the trailer likely limits the deployment of cell-matrix adhesion complexes.
source: It is conceivable that lower protrusive activity in the trailer limits the deployment of cell-matrix adhesion complexes.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observations.

claim: Cell-matrix adhesion in the trailer is probably needed to anchor the cell and allow for its hydrostatic pressure to push the leader.
source: However, cell-matrix adhesion in the trailer is probably needed to anchor the cell and allow for its hydrostatic pressure to push the leader.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on mechanical reasoning.

claim: One must invoke mechanisms whereby the leader suppresses protrusive activity in the trailer, while permitting the establishment of trailer cell-matrix adhesion in its path.
source: Therefore, one must invoke mechanisms whereby the leader suppresses protrusive activity in the trailer, while permitting the establishment of trailer cell-matrix adhesion in its path.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the observations.

claim: In Drosophila border cells, leader-driven suppression of protrusive activity in follower cells is mediated by Rac.
source: In Drosophila border cells, leader-driven suppression of protrusive activity in follower cells is mediated by Rac (Cai et al., 2014) and by Delta-Notch signaling between tip and stalk cells during angiogenesis (Aspalter et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: It is likely that similar 'front-to-back' mechanisms govern the collective distribution of protrusions, and by extension cell-matrix adhesion complexes, in cardiopharyngeal progenitors.
source: It is thus likely that similar 'front-to-back' mechanisms govern the collective distribution of protrusions, and by extension cell-matrix adhesion complexes, in cardiopharyngeal progenitors.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on comparison to other systems.

claim: Both computational simulations and live imaging indicated that the instantaneous directionality of single cells fluctuates more than that of cell pairs.
source: Specifically, both computational simulations and live imaging indicated that the instantaneous directionality of single cells fluctuates more than that of cell pairs.
evidence: This claim is supported by both computational and experimental results.

claim: Polarized cell pairs are more persistent than single cells.
source: In other words, polarized cell pairs are more persistent.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined computational and experimental results.

claim: It is possible that cell pairs are better at buffering the noise inherent to navigating a complex and changing environment, in part by distributing interactions over greater surfaces, and integrating guidance cues more accurately.
source: It is possible that cell pairs are better at buffering the noise inherent to navigating a complex and changing environment, in part by distributing interactions over greater surfaces, and integrating guidance cues more accurately.
evidence: This is a hypothesis to explain the observed persistence.

claim: Supracellular organization determines the outcome of interactions with surrounding tissues during migration.
source: Finally, our observations indicate that supracellular organization determines the outcome of interactions with surrounding tissues during migration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined computational and experimental results.

claim: TVC pairs migrate onto the extracellular matrix (ECM) associated with the basal lamina of the ventral trunk epidermis, which presumably offers a stiff substrate permitting traction forces.
source: We previously determined that TVC pairs migrate onto the extracellular matrix (ECM) associated with the basal lamina of the ventral trunk epidermis (Bernadskaya et al., 2019), which presumably offers a stiff substrate permitting traction forces.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work and includes a hypothesis about substrate properties.

claim: A specific collagen, col9-a1, secreted from the trunk endoderm is deposited onto the ECM and necessary for TVC-matrix adhesion and collective polarity.
source: Of note, a specific collagen, col9-a1, secreted from the trunk endoderm is deposited onto the ECM and necessary for TVC-matrix adhesion and collective polarity (Bernadskaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The trunk endoderm resists deformation by migrating TVCs, which can nonetheless move forward by aligning and joining forces to push against and deform endodermal cells to penetrate the extracellular space.
source: Here, we find that the trunk endoderm resists deformation by migrating TVCs, which can nonetheless move forward by aligning and joining forces to push against and deform endodermal cells to penetrate the extracellular space.
evidence: This claim is supported by the combined computational and experimental results.

claim: Combined simulations and experimental observations suggest an effect of supracellular organization on the inter-tissue balance of forces that determine morphogenesis in the embryo.
source: Our combined simulations and experimental observations thus suggest an effect of supracellular organization on the inter-tissue balance of forces that determine morphogenesis in the embryo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined computational and experimental results.
